items.title: Linking Event-sequence Data Claims to Analytic Provenance in Chatbots: Technique and Evaluation
items.abstract: Chatbots are increasingly used to analyze temporal event sequences of which website clickstreams are among the most common. Explanations are essential for understanding claims about event-sequence data. However, existing systems often require programming expertise to interpret these explanations and fail to explain the data processes underlying the data claims. We introduce a technique for linking a data claim to its analytic provenance (i.e., the analytic steps and results that produced it). It has two components: a reference table that records analytic steps and results in addressable cells, and a citation format that binds each claim to one or more cells. To operationalize this technique for clickstream analysis, we curated a set of analytic operations for clickstream analysis, organized them through a pivot-table abstraction, and developed tools that an AI agent can invoke to create a reference table and assemble a natural language response with cited data claims. To evaluate how citations affect users' assessment of data claims, we conducted two crowdsourced experiments with 90 participants each. The experiments showed that participants perceived correct data claims to be more accurate with citations when compared with no explanations, and that they perceived incorrect data claims to be less accurate with citations when compared with code and no explanations.

items.title: Making information behavior explicit in situation awareness
items.abstract: Situation awareness is fundamental to effective decision making in dynamic, uncertain, and information‐rich environments. While Endsley's three‐level situation awareness model introduced in 1995 defines the functions of perception, comprehension, and projection, the recurring information behaviors through which awareness is developed, maintained, and revised remain comparatively underspecified. This paper develops a conceptual framework integrating situation awareness and information behavior theories. The framework identifies and links triggers, information behaviors, evaluative judgments, and outcomes through four recurring mechanisms that explain how actors recognize information deficiencies, engage with and evaluate information, revise understanding, and determine whether understanding is sufficient for action. The framework extends existing situation awareness models by providing greater behavioral specificity while retaining Endsley's recursive conception of situation awareness. Six theoretical propositions are derived from the framework to guide future empirical research, and the framework identifies implications for communication and information systems. Collectively, the paper provides a more behaviorally grounded explanation of how situation awareness is maintained and revised in complex socio‐technical environments.

items.title: Repetition bias in self-directed learning
items.abstract: Self-directed learning is a major part of individual knowledge formation. People often autonomously organize their own learning into "blocks": they practice a certain task for some continuous stretch of time, then switch to another task for another period of time, and so on. Yet current models of intrinsic motivation highlighting epistemic factors such as novelty, competence, and learning progress make various predictions about the extent to which learners block, as opposed to interleaving, their practice. In this study, we demonstrate that people tend to block in a multi-task setting where existing models of intrinsic motivation based on epistemic factors make ambiguous predictions. We show that while epistemic factors can partially explain blocking, a simple repetition bias substantially improves our ability to predict choices.

items.title: THE ROLE OF ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE SYSTEMS IN DEVELOPING THE CREATIVE AND INTELLECTUAL POTENTIAL OF YOUNG SPECIALISTS: THE CASE OF IN-SERVICE TRAINING IN THE MINING AND GEOLOGY SECTOR OF UZBEKISTAN
items.abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is entering professional practice and adult learning rapidly, yet its effect on the creative and intellectual potential of young specialists is contested: AI can personalise learning and stimulate idea generation, but uncritical reliance may encourage cognitive offloading and weaken independent reasoning. This study examines how AI systems can strengthen, rather than replace, the independent thinking of young professionals, taking in-service training in Uzbekistan’s mining and geology sector as a case. A qualitative, document-based design combined national regulations, international guidance, peer-reviewed literature from a structured search of Scopus, Web of Science, and Google Scholar (2019–2026), and institutional records; 35 sources were analysed. Five educational functions of AI were identified: personalised learning, intelligent tutoring, simulation, generative assistance, and data analysis. A matrix links each function to its contribution, principal risk, and pedagogical safeguard, and four principles of “human-controlled AI” are proposed: transparency, verifiability, accountability, and developmental use. Mapping a sectoral AI course against the matrix showed an emphasis on generative content creation, with data analysis and tutoring underdeveloped; a three-module structure covering AI literacy, creative work with generative tools, and geological data analysis is therefore proposed. The findings are conceptual and require empirical validation with trainee-level measures.

items.title: Workplace AI Trust: Scale Development, Preliminary Psychometric Validation, and Associations with Employee AI Experience
items.abstract: As artificial intelligence becomes increasingly embedded in work, there is a need to understand employees’ beliefs about whether it can be relied upon in occupational settings. This study developed an eight-item Workplace AI Trust Scale and examined its preliminary measurement properties and associations with workplace AI experience. Polish working adults completed an online questionnaire, and separate randomly selected subsamples were used for exploratory and confirmatory factor analyses. The findings supported a common factor underlying the trust items and their empirical distinction from a supplementary distrust block. Internal consistency was high, although model fit was not uniformly favorable across all analyses. Changes in scaled fit indices provided qualified support for equal thresholds and loadings across exposure groups, although concerns about configural fit remained. Direct AI use was positively associated with trust, whereas the association with usage frequency was less consistent across analytical specifications. The reported presence of an organizational AI policy showed no statistically significant association with trust. Including the trust score improved average classification performance for AI-use frequency, but overall predictive performance remained limited. The findings support further investigation of the scale as a research instrument, while leaving its external convergent validity, broader discriminant validity, and suitability for group comparisons to be established.

items.title: Complementarity without ground truth?
items.abstract: Human-AI complementarity captures the idea that a human assisted by an AI system can outperform both the human and the AI acting alone. In prediction tasks, this improvement is assessed against ground truth labels produced through a reference construction procedure and intended to represent the state of affairs to be predicted. Many human-AI interactions, including those where medical AI provides treatment recommendations, however, concern tasks other than predicting what obtains. Their relevant output concerns adequacy relative to a practical goal and depends on several evaluative dimensions. In this work, we examine the ground truth dependence of complementarity and extend it to human-AI interactions where ground truth is not the appropriate reference. We show that tasks beyond prediction can still admit a reference construction procedure that generates adequacy labels. We develop a route for extending complementarity to such settings. It replaces ground truth labels with context-dependent adequacy labels generated through a two-step scoring methodology inspired by multi-criteria decision analysis frameworks in healthcare and it makes the normative choices underlying reference construction explicit. Because the construction of adequacy labels embeds evaluative choices, we draw methodological inspiration from computational reliabilism to identify technical, scientific, and social factors relevant to supporting their construction. Our approach expands the empirical study of human-AI complementarity beyond prediction tasks, enabling its quantitative evaluation in decision-support settings where ground truth is not the appropriate evaluative reference.

items.title: Early Signals of Problematic AI Use: The Longitudinal Roles of Motivation and Emotional Engagement
items.abstract: Longitudinal evidence about the psychological impact of conversational AI use remains scarce. We report a survey study of 114 adults who reported their level of problematic AI use one year after reporting their motivations (for escape, social, entertainment, and instrumental reasons) for engaging with AI. We found high levels of AI motivation of all types predicted later problematic AI use, especially when participants turned to AI for managing their feelings and overcoming difficulties. Our findings imply that AI motivation could be used as an early warning signal of potential problematic use, especially if individuals engage with AI for emotional purposes over time.

items.title: Enhancing Academic Productivity Through Artificial Intelligence: The Mediating Role of AI Literacy Among Malaysian University Students
items.abstract: The swift adoption of generative artificial intelligence (AI) in higher education has transformed student learning, presenting unparalleled opportunities for automated drafting, syntactic polish, and literature synthesis, while introducing profound vulnerabilities regarding algorithmic hallucinations, cognitive offloading, and threats to academic integrity. This conceptual paper addresses critical gaps in technology acceptance literature by proposing an integrative model that positions AI literacy as a pivotal cognitive and evaluative mediating mechanism between multidimensional AI usage and academic productivity. Grounded in the Technology Acceptance Model (TAM), Cognitive Load Theory (CLT), and contemporary AI literacy frameworks, the paper decouples raw technological interaction from substantive educational attainment. We demonstrate that while system usage directly enhances operational task completion velocity, substantive scholarly productivity—defined by analytical depth, critical rigor, and epistemic accuracy—depends upon multidimensional AI literacy (technical understanding, effective prompting, critical output evaluation, and ethical reflexivity). Four refined theoretical propositions are formulated, accounting for competing explanatory mediators (such as academic motivation, prior academic achievement, and institutional support) and contextual moderating boundaries (academic discipline, year of study, and premium tool access). To bridge conceptual theory and empirical practice, operational definitions and a comprehensive measurement item pool are provided alongside an illustrative dual-scenario analysis. Finally, specific contextual considerations for Malaysian higher education, an expanded discussion of germane load reduction hazards, a structured limitations section, and a rigorous time-lagged PLS-SEM empirical validation blueprint are detailed for future researchers, educators, and university administrators

items.title: Exploring performance and trust in autonomous surgical robotic systems: the role of visuo-haptic guidance
items.abstract: PURPOSE: Incorporating task-level autonomy into teleoperation systems for robot assisted laparoscopic surgery requires operators to effectively manage transitions from task-level autonomy to teleoperation control, particularly during system failures. This study investigated the impact of the level of guidance during take-over situations on participants' performance and their trust in the teleoperation system. METHODS: N = 34 students, unfamiliar with the system and task, performed a ring transfer task under two conditions: visual guidance, where they monitored the system visually, and visuo-haptic guidance, where they also received haptic feedback by holding the input device as the system operated in task-level autonomy. During some trials, system failures occurred, requiring participants to take over control. RESULTS: Results showed that participants noticed system failures faster with visuo-haptic guidance compared to visual guidance. Although visuo-haptic guidance did not improve task completion times or accuracy during task completion, it led to significantly higher trust in the teleoperation system and a stronger sense of perceived control. However, participants also reported higher physical demand and effort under visuo-haptic guidance, indicating an increased workload in this condition. CONCLUSION: In conclusion, these findings reveal important trade-offs of the influence of haptic guidance during human oversight of teleoperated autonomous systems.

items.title: Neurofeedback Beyond the Clinic: A Scoping Review of EEG-Driven VR and MR Systems in Sport, Education, Professional Training, and Consumer Wellness
items.abstract: Neurofeedback delivered through virtual and mixed reality has moved out of the clinic into sport, classroom, workplace-training, and consumer-wellness settings, but these four streams of literatures grow in near-isolation and cite one another rarely. We set out to read them against one technical grid, and report both what the grid shows and where the published reports do not fill it in. Reporting follows the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews, with PRISMA 2020 flow accounting. A Scopus search run on 12 May 2026 returned 131 records; 116 unique records were screened, 66 full texts were assessed, and 34 studies were retained, 32 from the database arm and two recovered by backward citation chasing. An independent second reviewer re-applied the eligibility criteria to the full text of every retained study. Eligibility was confirmed for 27 studies, which form the main analysis set, and could not be confirmed for seven, which are reported separately and enter only the sensitivity analyses. Consumer wellness supplies 18 of the 27 studies, education seven, and sport and professional training one each. Two reports are conceptual or architectural and are held out of every quantitative summary, leaving 25 empirical reports. Of those 25, the targeted outcome is stated in all 25 and the delivery medium in 21, but only 15 describe the EEG-to-environment coupling clearly enough to be classified as closed-loop, and only eight name the EEG feature used as the online control variable. Both counts are lower bounds on the corresponding properties of the systems, not point estimates. None of the seven records of unconfirmed eligibility discloses either field, so including them leaves both counts, and the conclusions drawn from them, as they are. No report could be classified as open-loop on affirmative evidence. A sensitivity search screened in duplicate, which dropped the machine-learning negation, the year bound, and the domain vocabulary (372 records; Cohen’s κ=0.66 at title and abstract), yielded 18 further eligible studies, and a uniform re-assessment of the contextual studies added 2 more. The search extends coverage and tests the robustness of the findings to the search strategy; it cannot be used to validate the full-text exclusions of the original search, because the identities of the excluded reports were not retained. In that set, 14 of 17 empirical reports name the control feature, which locates the reporting deficit in the application-oriented literature rather than in EEG-driven immersive feedback as a whole. Four of the eight disclosed control variables in the main corpus are alpha-band measures, and none of the eight comes from sport or education. The question most often asked of this literature, namely how many of these systems genuinely close the loop, therefore cannot be answered from the application-oriented record as it stands. We set out a five-field minimum reporting set that would make it answerable, and we propose, as a hypothesis for future testing rather than as a finding of this review, that the scarcity of EEG markers surviving promotion from offline correlate to online control variable is the constraint that organizes the field. The key charted fields of all 34 retained studies were re-assessed by the independent second reviewer; agreement was fair for loop topology (κ=0.40) and at chance for whether the control feature is named, because the second reviewer consistently read the reports more permissively than the written rules allow.

items.title: Public perceptions of infrastructural digital nudging: an experience-based study in a quasi-public setting
items.abstract: Digital nudging increasingly shapes behavior, impressions, and decision-making in public spaces. However, existing empirical research has largely focused on nudging in relation to individualized decision-making, offering limited insight into how diverse publics interpret such technologies when embedded in public infrastructures—what we refer to here as infrastructural digital nudging. In such settings, the influence of digital nudging may become less visible and less easily avoidable, while asymmetries between those who design the technology and those who encounter it may become more consequential. These conditions, together with the possibility that public expectations and social implications extend beyond expert-defined frameworks, highlight the need for early engagement. In this study, we investigate public perceptions of infrastructural digital nudging based on multi-display signage through a demonstration conducted at a national science museum in Japan. We used a convergent mixed-methods design that combined quantitative analyses of structured questionnaire responses with qualitative analyses of open-ended questionnaire responses and sticky notes. This research design enabled both statistical analysis and fine-grained interpretation of participants’ concerns, interests, and imagined uses. Our results show that, at an aggregate level, participants prioritized understanding the technology’s mechanisms, purposes, and social impacts over canonical ethical categories such as autonomy and transparency. However, qualitative analyses revealed considerable heterogeneity: some participants expressed strong concerns about unconscious influence, manipulation, and misuse. Co-occurrence analyses further indicated that participants’ evaluations were structured around different perspectives, including science-focused assessment and social concerns. These findings suggest that public perceptions of infrastructural digital nudging are heterogeneous and organized around multiple perspectives, not reducible to expert-defined categories. This underscores the importance of empirically examining how such technologies are interpreted when encountered in environments approximating real-world situations.

items.title: Too Big to Inspect? Ethically Auditing Large Datasets Through Small Samples
items.abstract: Big techs and researchers increasingly claim that their training datasets are too large to inspect for bias and ethical problems. However, in the race to build ever-large models, they have relied on automated web scraping and no human curation. Datasets built this way absorb the stereotypes, exclusionary norms, and historical prejudices of their sources, and the models trained on them can reproduce and amplify those patterns. Because manually auditing billions of samples is humanly impossible, we need practical, effective methods to identify biases in these datasets. This paper studies the feasibility of ethically auditing large datasets through small samples and proposes a practical method for identifying structural biases by applying AI Ethics Tools (AIETs) to random samples. We applied Datasheets for Datasets, Data Statements, Data Nutrition Labels, and Data Cards to a 1% sample of Framed Multi30K, and Datasheets for Datasets to two 0.00006% samples of relaion2B-en-research-safe. Our results show that evaluating small samples with AIETs can reveal ethical problems, structural biases, and technical inconsistencies. Although industry practice assumes that identifying problems requires analyzing the entire dataset, we show that a random subset supports a viable qualitative analysis without overwhelming computational or human resources. Demonstrating that a dataset is biased does not require examining every instance: if a bias appears in a random sample, it is a flaw of the creation process. The AIETs' questions acted as provocateurs, evoking different perspectives and analysis methods for the same dataset, but the analysis and its results depended fundamentally on the human factor. We hope these findings contribute to urgent public discussions about ethics, transparency, accountability, and AI regulation by offering a practical pathway for responsibly auditing massive datasets.

items.title: Validation and Evacuee Modeling of Virtual Robot-guided Emergency Evacuation Experiments
items.abstract: Virtual Reality (VR) is an increasingly common tool for investigating human responses to emergency situations. Nonetheless, studies validating and comparing human subject behavior during real world emergencies to their responses in VR are notably rare, and no prior studies have validated whether human emergency responses to guidance from a robot are comparable in VR versus the real world. In the present pre-registered study, we used VR to replicate a previous robot-guided emergency evacuation study conducted in the real world and compared human subject behavior in matched physical and virtual environments. In both environments, human subjects were asked to follow a robot to a location and to then read an article. While reading, a fire alarm sounds. The robot then attempted to guide them to a distant, unfamiliar exit rather than a nearby and familiar exit. We observed close correspondences between evacuee exit choice (the robot’s distant exit versus closer exits), evacuation time, and self-reported trust in the robot between the VR and physical environments. We further demonstrate that data collected in virtual reality can be used to create accurate motion models (mean positional error of 0.42 meters) predicting evacuee trajectories and locations in the physical environment.

items.title: A lightweight convolutional neural network for target detection in an edge environment
items.abstract: This paper proposes a novel, lightweight convolutional neural network (CNN) designed for edge device deployment. The CNN is developed to recognize and classify threats or targets of interest. The model is equipped with a real-time hotspot detection algorithm, which enables it to process information quickly and accurately, resulting in improved inference time of up to 20 fps and a detection range of more than 400 meters with typical thermal situational awareness sensors. The proposed CNN has been rigorously tested and validated to demonstrate its high accuracy, sensitivity, and low false positive rate, providing a reliable solution for edge devices to detect potential targets. Additionally, the lightweight design of the CNN allows for easy deployment, making it an ideal solution for extending the security bubble for edge devices. The proposed model can be used for a variety of applications, including surveillance, security, and object recognition.

items.title: A Novel Dual-Function Face-Shield Prototype Integrating an On-Demand Hand-Sanitiser Reservoir: Design and Preliminary Benchtop Evaluation
items.abstract: Background and Objectives: Rapid hand hygiene is difficult to maintain during uninterrupted patient care. We designed and performed a preliminary benchtop evaluation of a proof-of-concept face-shield prototype integrating an on-demand disinfectant reservoir. Materials and Methods: A dual-function wearable system was built from a PETG visor (230 × 230 mm, 0.20 mm) and modular reservoirs (25, 50, 75, 100 mL). Five complete prototype units were fabricated under the same manufacturing conditions: two separate physical units with 100 mL reservoirs (Units A and B) and one unit each with 75, 50, and 25 mL reservoirs. Functional and mechanical testing was performed across the two 100 mL units, with shared and unit-specific endpoints; chemical compatibility was evaluated using dedicated PETG specimens, while ergonomic assessment was limited to biomechanical modelling. Disinfectant density (Mikrozid AF Liquid) was measured (0.875 ± 0.002 g/mL, n = 5) to convert dispensed mass to volume. The valve delivered 3.08 ± 0.21 mL/activation (CV 6.8%, n = 60; 30/unit, single fill, no refilling). Results: The system weighed 103.3 g empty and 190.8 g filled with 100.0 mL of disinfectant (87.5 g disinfectant mass). Recalculated cervical torque (τ = m × g × r; baseline: 0.084 N·m) was 0.118 N·m for the empty-reservoir configuration (+40.6%) and 0.252 N·m for the filled configuration (+199.9%). No continuous leakage occurred (mass loss < 0.1 g), retention exceeded 10 N in all directions, and PETG remained stable after 14-day immersion and 50 wiping cycles. Estimated cost was €10–20/unit. Conclusions: This proof-of-concept supports the technical feasibility of integrating a face-shield platform with immediate access to hand sanitisation in one reusable device, without establishing standards-based protective performance. The small number of separate physical prototypes used for functional testing (two 100 mL units), together with the absence of microbiological, optical-standard and human-factor validation, limits generalisability. Human-participant, microbiological, ergonomic and clinical usability studies are required before clinical implementation. A conceptual touchless valve is proposed for future work.

items.title: Barriers to Social Media Engagement Among People With Dementia: A Qualitative Survey
items.abstract: Social media can offer benefits for people with dementia, including enhanced social connectivity, peer support, and access to information. However, digital exclusion remains an issue, and little is known about factors that deter engagement. This study explored barriers to social media use from the perspectives of people with dementia and their unpaid carers. An online survey was completed by 227 participants (179 carers; 48 people with dementia), including questions about attitudes toward social media. Reflexive thematic analysis of open responses generated six themes: (1) Perceived value of social media; (2) Generational and age-limiting beliefs; (3) Digital access and literacy; (4) Perceived (un)safety of social media; (5) Symptoms of dementia; (6) Heavy caring loads. Social, cognitive, and technological factors perpetuate exclusion from social media among people with dementia. Addressing these barriers requires improved digital access, literacy, and safety, alongside more inclusive platform design and support for carers facilitating engagement.

items.title: Conversational Artificial Intelligence in Community Care: A Scoping Review
items.abstract: The strategic shift toward community-based healthcare, away from hospital settings, is a policy priority internationally. Conversational artificial intelligence (CAI) may support this transition, yet its practical applications remain underexplored. This scoping review maps CAI capabilities and their configuration within community care. We searched PubMed, the ACM Digital Library, and selected grey-literature sources for studies published from January 2023 to June 2025. Of 551 records identified, 29 studies were included. We identified 20 capabilities across five functional domains: Understand (n = 5), Transform (n = 3), Remember (n = 3), Generate (n = 5), and Act (n = 4). Findings suggest that CAI extends rather than replaces human care, supporting access, ongoing engagement, and care coordination. Multi-party and expert-in-the-loop designs emerged as recurring implementation strategies. They also surface design tensions, including tradeoffs between reliability and conversational flexibility, and between the benefits of long-term memory and associated privacy risks. The resulting capability-centered taxonomy offers accessible framework for integrating CAI into community care settings.

items.title: Determining Voice Control Boundaries for in-Vehicle Functions: A User-Engineer-Expert Assessment Framework
items.abstract: Efficiently adapting voice control functions in smart vehicles remains a practical challenge in human-computer interaction. This study established a three-source, lightweight research system comprising user questionnaire survey (N = 326), engineer evaluation from the corporate sector (N = 12), and expert interviews from the industry (N = 8). A six-dimensional weighted adaptability assessment model(SWAAM) was designed (safety risk 30%, operational complexity 20%, usage frequency 15%, command clarity 15%, feedback requirements 10%, and technical feasibility 10%). Within 15 days, a systematic evaluation of 30 vehicle control functions was completed. The results indicate that user voice preference exhibits significant stratification: preference rates for high-frequency comfort functions such as navigation, air conditioning, and media exceed 98%, while preference rates for safety-critical functions such as driver assistance and chassis control are below 60%. Through triangulation validation, 15 items were identified for the whitelist (priority for release), 3 for the blacklist (prohibited from release), and 12 for the graylist (requiring scenario-based release, e.g., window control limited to speeds below 80 km/h, special scenario modes restricted to parking only). Expert consensus established safety red lines and design specifications, including “prohibition of voice control for core driving functions,” “adoption of the “action + object” command format,” and “requirement for secondary confirmation for safety-related functions.” The weighted total score across the six dimensions showed high consistency with the functional list (whitelist ≥ 7 points, blacklist <4.0 points), validating the model’s effectiveness. This method ensures scientific rigor while reducing the adaptation cycle to 15 days. It provides a practical, lightweight framework for rapid iteration in mass-production voice interaction projects.

items.title: Efficient Sensor Configuration for Accelerometer-Based Silent Speech Interfaces: Regionally Distributed Sensor Placement Strategy Considering Articulatory Dynamics
items.abstract: Silent speech interfaces (SSIs) decode articulatory activity without audible speech. Although accelerometer-based SSIs can capture facial and neck movements in compact wearable setups, accelerometer-specific sensor placement has not been systematically examined. This study evaluated all combinations of ten accelerometers across the lower face and neck in a 100 English word silent speech classification task with 20 participants. Subject-dependent classification was performed using a convolutional neural network followed by a bidirectional long short-term memory network. Accuracy improved as the number of sensors increased, reaching a plateau with five sensors. At this point, Sensors 1 and 7, positioned over the upper and lower labial regions, Sensors 4 and 8, located bilaterally along the buccal-mandibular region, and Sensor 5, placed over the left submental region beneath the chin, achieved the highest accuracy of 92.30 ± 4.64% and were selected as the efficient configuration. These five sensors consistently ranked among the most informative locations in standalone performance, perturbation-based explainability, and sensor ablation analyses, indicating that they contributed unique and influential articulatory information. Regional coverage comparisons showed that configurations spanning broader functional articulatory regions outperformed those with more restricted coverage. This placement strategy was further validated using an independent 100-word vocabulary, demonstrating that broad regional coverage remained advantageous despite slight changes in the optimal sensor identities. A practical three-sensor configuration based on this strategy achieved approximately 90% recognition accuracy while substantially reducing hardware complexity. Together, these results support regionally distributed sensor placement as a design strategy for capturing complementary articulatory information in compact accelerometer-based SSI systems.

items.title: ElasticGS: Pose-Aware Dynamic Gaussian Adaptation for Geometry-Consistent Human Digital Twin Reconstruction from Monocular Video
items.abstract: Vision-based 3D sensing provides an effective approach for constructing human-centric digital twins in applications such as ergonomic assessment and human-robot collaboration. However, reconstructing reliable dynamic human digital twins from visual sensor observations remains challenging due to large articulated deformation, which often causes surface discontinuities in existing 3D Gaussian Splatting (3DGS)-based human avatars. Although current methods achieve high image-level rendering quality, their Gaussian primitives are not explicitly adapted to pose-induced surface deformation, resulting in cracks and holes during motion. In this work, we propose ElasticGS, a geometry-consistent human digital twin reconstruction framework for vision-based 3D sensing. ElasticGS introduces a training-free Pose-Aware Dynamic Covariance Adaptation strategy, which dynamically adjusts the rotation and anisotropic scale of Gaussian primitives according to local human surface deformation. Specifically, localized Principal Component Analysis (PCA) is performed on deformed SMPL-X mesh neighborhoods to estimate surface stretching directions and magnitudes, enabling Gaussian representations to maintain continuous surface coverage under complex poses. Furthermore, we propose the Avatar Surface Integrity Score (ASIS), a reference-free metric that evaluates structural completeness and surface compactness of reconstructed human avatars without requiring pixel-aligned ground truth. Experiments on the X-Humans, AvatarReX, and People-Snapshot datasets demonstrate that ElasticGS significantly improves surface integrity while maintaining competitive image-level sensing consistency. Compared with ExAvatar, ElasticGS maintains satisfactory rendering quality while improving ASIS from 0.741 to 0.961 on X-Humans, from 0.871 to 0.949 on AvatarReX, and from 0.874 to 0.952 on People-Snapshot. These results demonstrate the effectiveness of pose-aware covariance adaptation for robust human digital twin reconstruction in vision-based 3D sensing systems.

items.title: Encoding Memory in World Models with Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning
items.abstract: Model-based reinforcement learning (MBRL) approaches have demonstrated strong performance across diverse domains in recent years, learning accurate world models from agent trajectories. However, despite this progress, current approaches still struggle to surpass human performance on tasks that require long-term memory and planning. In this work, we address the problem of long-term memory in MBRL by moving beyond the commonly studied paradigm of architecture design. We introduce Test-Time Model-Based Reinforcement Learning (TT-MBRL), using gradient descent at test time to encode the memory of episode observations into world model parameters. This enables the agent to learn a distinct world model for each episode, improving memory capabilities compared to traditional approaches that solely rely on contextual memory. We first establish a proof of concept on a simplified two-dimensional variant of the Memory Maze environment, which we refer to as Memory Maze 2D, showing consistent improvements across different world model architectures. We then demonstrate the effectiveness of TT-MBRL in the 3D domain, achieving new state-of-the-art results on the Memory Maze benchmark. Finally, we show that TT-MBRL maintains strong performance on non-memory benchmarks such as DeepMind Control and Atari 100k.

items.title: From Vibe to Code—and Back: Lexical Oscillation in the Formation of Design Intent with Generative AI
items.abstract: Generative AI design tools make natural-language prompts a starting point for design, placing new articulation demands on designers. Rather than treating prompts as the transmission of preexisting intent, we ask how design intent is formed through situated interaction with AI. Five expert UI/UX designers (11–20 years’ experience, M = 15.4) designed landing-page hero sections with a generative AI tool, recorded through think-aloud and retrospective interviews. Using reflexive thematic analysis, we treated lexical granularity (L1 vibe, L2 design-domain, L3 operational language) as a sensitizing lens. Rather than moving from vibe to code unidirectionally, designers showed lexical oscillation, including returns from operational specificity to ambiguity. Mismatches with AI outputs became occasions to reconsider what they meant, and engagement shifted from instruction to consultation. One non-oscillating trajectory—a negative case—suggested conceptual misalignment as a tentative boundary. We position AI as a non-neutral generative interlocutor and ambiguity as a resource for design judgment.

items.title: Hepatitis B susceptibility, infection and vaccine-induced immunity among health personnel in Sokoto, Nigeria: a cross-sectional serological study
items.abstract: Background Health personnel in Nigeria have a high occupational risk of hepatitis B virus (HBV) infection, and vaccination status is usually established by self-report. The extent to which reported vaccination corresponds to serological protection has not been measured in northern Nigeria. We described HBV infection and immunity among health personnel, compared self-reported vaccination with serological markers and identified factors associated with vaccine-induced immunity, natural immunity and current infection. Methods We conducted an analytical cross-sectional serological study of 473 health personnel selected by multistage sampling from primary, secondary and tertiary facilities in Sokoto State between January and March 2023. An interviewer-administered semi-structured questionnaire was completed, and serum was tested for HBsAg, anti-HBs, anti-HBc, HBeAg and anti-HBe with a five-panel rapid test. Firth penalised logistic regression was used for each outcome. Results Current infection (HBsAg positive) was found in 7.8% (n = 37; 95% CI: 5.7–10.6) and evidence of any past or current infection in 17.1% (n = 81). Anti-HBs was detected in 16.5% (n = 78): 12.3% (n = 58) had vaccine-induced and 4.2% (n = 20) natural immunity, while 70.6% (n = 334) had no serological marker. Self-reported vaccination had a positive predictive value of 24.3% for vaccine-induced immunity (κ = 0.16). Among 96 participants who reported three or more doses, 69.8% (n = 67) had no detectable anti-HBs and six were HBsAg positive. Vaccine-induced immunity was associated with three or more reported doses (aOR 2.90; 95% CI: 1.37–6.22), positive attitude (aOR 1.98; 95% CI: 1.01–3.90), an employer request for vaccination status (aOR 2.05; 95% CI: 1.03–3.97) and insertion of tubes or catheters (aOR 2.75; 95% CI: 1.08–6.93). Natural immunity was more frequent in primary facilities (aOR 4.84; 95% CI: 1.56–15.30). Current infection was not associated with occupational exposures and was less frequent after more than 10 years of practice (aOR 0.23; 95% CI: 0.06–0.84). Conclusions Most health personnel in Sokoto had no serological protection against HBV, and self-reported vaccination overstated protection. Screening for HBsAg and anti-HBs at recruitment, documented vaccination with post-vaccination testing, and referral of infected staff for care should be part of routine occupational health services.

items.title: Integrated Cognitive Workload and Musculoskeletal Exposure Modeling for Adaptive Ergonomic Work Design
items.abstract: Cognitive workload, musculoskeletal exposure, fatigue, and limited recovery can jointly affect worker comfort and task performance. However, these factors are often assessed separately, limiting the evaluation of cumulative ergonomic risk over time. This study proposes an integrated ergonomic modeling framework that combines cognitive workload, physical exposure, fatigue accumulation, and recovery within a common assessment structure. Normalized state variables are used to calculate a composite ergonomic risk index, and a proposed multi objective optimization procedure provides a basis for examining alternative task schedules and recovery intervals. Illustrative scenarios compare low, moderate, and high combined demands under specified model assumptions. The proposed analytical design also specifies a procedure for future sensitivity analysis of workload intensity, exposure duration, recovery rate, and worker susceptibility. The illustrative values indicate that higher modeled cognitive workload, physical exposure, and fatigue correspond to greater composite risk under the specified weighting scheme. However, these values are hypothetical and do not represent observed worker data or verified simulation outputs. The framework provides a methodological basis for examining relationships between modeled ergonomic risk and task performance during work schedule planning. Further research should implement reproducible computational experiments, conduct sensitivity analyses, and validate model predictions against measured workload, physical exposure, fatigue, and performance data before practical application.

items.title: Perceived Crisis-Management Training Adequacy and Wellbeing Indicators Among Seafarers During the Red Sea Crisis: An Exploratory Survey
items.abstract: Global shipping carries over 80% of world trade, yet existing supply-chain-resilience theory models resilience at the level of the firm, node and network, without treating the workforce operating those nodes as a variable. This exploratory study addresses that gap using the 2023–2026 Red Sea/Houthi crisis as its empirical setting. A pilot-scale, cross-sectional online survey of 64 serving seafarers combined closed-ended items with qualitative content analysis of two open-text questions. Seafarers who had witnessed or been directly involved in a security incident rated STCW crisis-management training as less adequate for conflict-area risk than those without such exposure (Mann–Whitney U = 227.0, p = 0.007, r = 0.34), the only comparison that remained significant after Holm adjustment within its family of tests; Red Sea transit or Cape of Good Hope rerouting without an incident was not associated with lower ratings. Open-text responses identified situational information and realistic scenario-based drills, rather than generic compliance training, as the specific gap, and a minority questioned seafarers’ right to decline a high-risk voyage. Because fatigue and psychological distress could be captured only through single, non-validated items, findings on these outcomes are indicative only. Building on these results, the study proposes, as exploratory propositions for future testing rather than established relationships, two human-factor pathways through which geopolitical risk may affect operational resilience: a training-competence pathway and a retention/psychological-contract pathway. The study contributes hypothesis-generating evidence, gathered directly from an affected workforce, and derives practical and policy recommendations for STCW training content and seafarer consent protections.

items.title: Prevalence and Environmental Correlates of Back Pain among Schoolchildren in Maiduguri Metropolis, North-Eastern Nigeria: A Cross-Sectional Multi-Stage Survey
items.abstract: Background Low back pain (LBP) among adolescents represents a significant but understudied public health challenge in Sub-Saharan Africa. This study investigated the prevalence and multi-factorial determinants of LBP among secondary school students in Maiduguri Metropolis, North-Eastern Nigeria. Methods Using a multi-stage stratified sampling technique, this cross-sectional survey recruited 1,012 adolescents from both public and private schools. Participant demographics, commuting characteristics, carrying habits, and spinal pain histories were assessed via a validated questionnaire. Objective measurements of standing height, body mass, and absolute backpack weight were taken using calibrated equipment to determine relative load percentage (% body weight [%BW]). Statistical analyses included Spearman rank correlations and multivariable binary logistic regression to evaluate independent risk factors (aOR, 95 CI). Results Among analyzed respondents (N = 1,005), overall LBP prevalence was 55.6% (n = 559), with within-sex rates of 58.4% for males (272/466) and 53.2% for females (287/539). Unadjusted correlation analysis showed mild positive associations between pain severity and both absolute bag weight (r s = + 0.120, p < 0.001) and relative bag load (r s = + 0.103, p = 0.001). However, after multivariable adjustments (chi 2 = 28.44, p < 0.001), carrying loads > 10% BW failed to maintain independent statistical significance (aOR = 1.21, 95% CI: 0.91–1.61, p = 0.188). The principal independent determinants of LBP were female sex (aOR = 1.42, 95% CI: 1.08–1.87, p = 0.012), overweight/obese BMI (aOR = 1.54, 95% CI: 1.10–2.16, p = 0.011), and daily carriage times exceeding 30 minutes (aOR = 1.45, 95% CI: 1.09–1.93, p = 0.010). Conclusion Spinal discomfort is widespread among Nigerian secondary school students and driven by complex interactions. Isolated schoolbag weight is a weaker predictor of pain than physical exposure duration (> 30mins/day) and personal attributes (sex and BMI). Preventative school ergonomics should prioritize active transit planning and physical wellness over strict weight limits alone.

items.title: Process evaluation of a migrant-inclusive risk communication and community engagement intervention: lessons from the Health Handbook for Vietnamese Workers in Japan
items.abstract: BACKGROUND: Migrant workers in Japan face persistent barriers in accessing timely and culturally appropriate health information owing to language constraints, complex administrative systems, and fragmented risk communication channels. These challenges have been exacerbated during the COVID-19 pandemic, highlighting the need for migrant-inclusive risk communication and community engagement (RCCE). In response, the Government of Vietnam, the International Organization for Migration (IOM), and Japanese partners collaboratively developed the Health Handbook for Vietnamese Workers in Japan as a transnational RCCE intervention. METHODS: This study evaluates a process the development, dissemination, monitoring, and iterative adaptation of the Handbook. Multiple data sources were triangulated, including mixed-methods situation analyses, technical working group documentation, Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) assessment, digital analytics, and qualitative stakeholder feedback. Qualitative data were analysed using an inductive thematic approach. Themes generated from the data were subsequently interpreted in relation to RCCE principles and the social determinants of health framework to identify mechanisms relevant to the implementation of a migrant-inclusive RCCE. RESULTS: The evaluation identified three interrelated mechanisms that appeared to support migrant-inclusive RCCE: (1) addressing structural vulnerabilities; (2) deploying multichannel communication strategies tailored to migrants; and (3) engaging migrant communities and stakeholders. The Handbook was designed to provide practical health information, particularly on occupational health, healthcare navigation, and rights-related topics. Digital analytics showed an increased reach following collaboration with community-based platforms, while the Patient Education Materials Assessment Tool (PEMAT) assessment indicated high understandability (81.3%) but moderate actionability (66.7%), indicating a need for iterative revisions. The intervention provided a platform for multi-sectoral collaboration and supported the continuity of health messaging across the migration cycle. CONCLUSIONS: This study illustrates that migrant-inclusive RCCE, when implemented through participatory, multi-sectoral, and transnational approaches, may support more equitable access to health information and contribute to health system resilience. Integrating such approaches within national preparedness frameworks may strengthen effective emergency responses and help address the structural determinants that shape migrant health by influencing exposure to health risks, access to reliable information and essential services, and the ability to seek timely and appropriate care.

items.title: Recent Developments in Global Probabilistic Turbulence Forecast Products for Aeronautical Meteorology at Deutscher Wetterdienst
items.abstract: Atmospheric turbulence is a major hazard for commercial flight operations. As a result, reliable and easily interpretable meteorological forecast data for this hazard is paramount to the safety of aircraft, crew and passengers. To meet this requirement, Deutscher Wetterdienst (DWD) has further improved their forecast products by blending the traditional deterministic numerical weather prediction of the Eddy Dissipation Parameter (EDP) with the probabilistic forecast to exceed the severe turbulence threshold of the EDP from its operational ensemble prediction system (EPS). Building on those results and inspired by an agile co-design approach with key users, a turbulence advisory was conceived which condenses three-dimensional spatial information into two dimensions in order to further support situational awareness and complement traditional aeronautical meteorological charts. In this technical paper, the necessity for products of this kind is motivated and their design and specifications are briefly explained.

items.title: Revolutionising White‐Collar Help‐Seeking in Organisations: The Impact and Dynamics of Artificial Intelligence‐Driven Chatbots
items.abstract: This study explores how white‐collar workers perceive AI‐driven chatbots, and how affordances and constraints shape their help‐seeking behaviours. Help‐seeking is essential for learning and collaboration but is often limited by social barriers. Drawing on Affordance Theory, this research examines how technological and social affordances influence chatbot use. Based on 24 in‐depth interviews, conducted between May and December 2023, at the inception of ChatGPT's public diffusion, the study reveals that chatbots offer judgement‐free support for repetitive and informational tasks, fostering autonomy and bypassing interpersonal discomfort. However, concerns about trust, limited capabilities, surveillance and job security constrain adoption. Individual mindset and age, together with organisational culture (e.g., innovation climate), further influence use. Chatbots redefine help‐seeking as a human‐machine dynamic, complementing rather than replacing human support. The study highlights the importance of designing chatbot systems that align with user needs and workplace cultures. In doing so, it contributes to debates on algorithmic management and worker autonomy and offers practical implications for integrating AI tools to support knowledge sharing and collaboration in work environments.

items.title: xLightGCN: Explainable Graph Neural Network Based Recommendation Systems with Most Influential Peers
items.abstract: Recommendation systems, systems that predict a user's preference for items in order to curate that user's feed, are a ubiquitous and central feature in online social networks. While they are a central piece of our modern digital infrastructure, many modern approaches are opaque black boxes, making them difficult to audit, understand, and assess the trustworthiness of. In this paper we present an exact, graph-based approach for generating explanations for decisions made by recommendation systems. We argue that in the risk-sensitive sociotechnical context of user-facing AI such as recommendation systems, explainability is a key pillar for establishing the trustworthiness of models and validating their effectiveness. We propose a technique built on LightGCN-like architectures, an influential and popular class of recommendation models. We describe our approach and argue that it provides an appropriate assurance mechanism for these AI systems leading to specific advantages, including interpretable explanations and a theoretically guaranteed measure of explanation fidelity. We conclude by discussing limitations and directions for future research.

items.title: Technohybridism: Recursive Semantic Normalization in AI-Mediated Societies
items.abstract: Language-generating AI systems are no longer only objects of linguistic interaction: their outputs increasingly re-enter the communicative and institutional practices from which their training material was drawn. Drawing on social theory, social epistemology, and the philosophy of language, this article develops a sociotechnical account of that re-entry. We introduce recursive semantic normalization: the process through which machine-generated formulations, once recurrently taken up, evaluated, reused, and institutionally retained, participate in the reproduction and transformation of semantic regularities. Under the heading of technohybridism, we argue that the relevant unit of analysis is the hybrid semantic system, a recursively coupled configuration of human practices, computational generation, and institutional uptake. First, we distinguish the concept from neighbouring accounts, including model collapse, looping effects, machine habitus, machine culture, and the epistemology of AI testimony. Second, we develop an analytical model that separates generation, selection, uptake, and persistence and distinguishes machine-attributable change from change that would have occurred anyway. Third, we analyse uptake as routinized, institutionally diffused, and socially stratified practice and state conditions under which machine-derived regularities become norms. Fourth, we identify social-epistemic consequences: the laundering of provenance that weakens epistemic vigilance, the erosion of the cognitive diversity on which collective inquiry depends, and the narrowing of shared hermeneutical resources. An evidential ladder for empirical research follows. The account attributes no normative authority to machine outputs; what changes is the field within which human and institutional uptake operates.

items.title: FireOPS: A Human-Centric Emergency Operations Platform
items.abstract: Volunteer fire brigades rely on fragmented alerting channels and radio plus paper for situational awareness, hindering a shared common operational picture (COP). FireOPS integrates smartphone alerting, navigation, a live geospatial COP, a district resource-load overview and contextual manuals into a human-centric decision-support surface for commanders and responders, running on an edge + cloud architecture whose dual-channel provides source-level redundancy against failure of either the radio or the provincial server feed; delivery to smartphones still depends on the cloud core and mobile networks. This lessons-learned report presents the design rationale, positions FireOPS within emergency-response information systems research, and reports operational findings from a primary log extract of a major regional flood in 2024 and from the 2025 public app release. A feature-matrix comparison with DIVERA 24/7, blaulichtSMS and the LifeRescue prototype identifies COP, decision support and dual-ingestion redundancy as the main differentiators, and we map the operational gaps observed during the flood to concrete engineering responses, deployed or in active development.

items.title: Holistic Parallel Supervision for Expressive Speech to Speech Translation
items.abstract: Expressiveness is central to speech-to-speech translation (S2ST), yet existing datasets rarely align source and target speech jointly in content, prosody, timing, and speaker identity. Consequently, current systems often rely on indirect conditioning or transfer mechanisms. To obtain this supervision, we introduce a training-data construction strategy that combines professional dubbing, which provides human-performed correspondence in content, prosody, and timing, with multilingual voice conversion to reduce speaker mismatch. We evaluate this supervision using existing expressive S2ST systems and DirectS2ST, an end-to-end method developed in this work that predicts the complete target-speech representation directly from source speech. Experiments on English-German and English-Spanish show that holistic parallel supervision improves expressive realization across all evaluated systems. DirectS2ST exhibits the largest gains in content, prosody, timing, speaker similarity, and human-rated expressiveness. To our knowledge, this work provides the first systematic investigation of holistic parallel supervision for expressive S2ST.

items.title: AI Systems for Qualitative Data Interrogation (EpiChat) and Semi-Automated Coding (EpiCode)
items.abstract: Background: The Virage project collected approximately 800 one-hour interviews on rabies awareness, including transmission, disease progression, and vaccination. Manually searching, comparing, and coding this corpus would require substantial time and human resources. Objective: EpiChat and EpiCode were developed using large language models (LLMs) to support natural-language interrogation and thematic analysis of interview transcripts. Local LLMs were used to preserve data privacy, avoid sharing data with foreign cloud services, and eliminate token and subscription costs. Methods: EpiChat uses an LLM-based router to direct questions to three specialized pipelines. An SQL pipeline translates structured metadata questions into database queries. For questions regarding counts or proportions, a map-reduce pipeline examines each interview independently and aggregates the results. Explanatory questions are handled using Retrieval-Augmented Generation (RAG). Because conventional RAG retrieves only the highest-ranked passages across the corpus, it may overlook rare perspectives that are important to qualitative research. To address this, EpiChat introduces a deep search mode that formulates the question as a quotation and searches for it into each interview. Verified quotations from matching interviews are then combined into a single response with source citations. EpiCode supports qualitative coding by matching transcript segments to a two-level codebook of main codes and subcodes. Each suggested code includes a model-generated confidence score, supporting quotation, and brief rationale. When no existing code adequately represents the content, the system proposes a new code. All suggestions require researcher review and approval. Results: Preliminary runtime measurements showed that EpiChat processed an interview-level query in approximately four seconds per interview, while EpiCode generated code suggestions for an entire interview in around three minutes. Conclusion: EpiChat and EpiCode provide a privacy-preserving, locally deployed platform for AI-assisted qualitative analysis. Future work will compare AI-generated codebooks with human-developed codebooks and evaluate whether EpiChat produces answers consistent with findings derived from manual coding. items.title: Assessing bias in the use of large language models in healthcare: a systematic review
items.abstract: Abstract The rapid advancement of Large Language Models (LLMs) has driven their growing adoption across domains, including healthcare. However, these models risk amplifying existing healthcare disparities. This systematic review synthesizes the existing literature on bias assessment in LLMs applied within the healthcare domain. We searched six databases, namely, Scopus, PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, IEEE Xplore, and the ACM Digital Library, for studies published between January 2020 and May 2025, with the final search conducted on 16 May 2025. Retrieved records were screened according to predefined criteria, resulting in 74 included articles. Methodological quality was assessed using the Joanna Briggs Institute Critical Appraisal Checklist for Analytical Cross-Sectional Studies. Owing to methodological heterogeneity, findings were described narratively. LLMs were applied across various healthcare contexts, most notably in medical question answering. Bias assessment methods ranged from human evaluations to statistical analyses, while only 13.5% of the included studies implemented mitigation strategies, which were primarily prompt-based. Overall, 87.8% of the studies reported evidence of bias, with demographic bias being the most commonly investigated bias type. The included studies were of predominantly high quality with minimal risk of bias. The findings indicate that bias remains prevalent in LLM healthcare outputs, highlighting a critical challenge to their equitable and responsible deployment. Future studies should prioritize robust bias evaluation and the implementation of effective bias mitigation strategies to support the safe integration of LLMs into healthcare.

items.title: CATNAP: Celltype Annotation by Taxonomy of Nested Adaptive Predictors
items.abstract: Background: Single-cell RNA-seq has transformed biological research by resolving cellular heterogeneity invisible to bulk approaches, revealing fine cell types, elucidating host responses to infection, vaccination, and disease. Objectives: Hierarchical annotation models mirror the hierarchical definition of cell types, but existing tools fix a single classifier family and often feature space across all nodes. We offer a flexible hierarchical cell type annotation framework with a unified interface, supporting several classification methods, user-defined cell-types, node-specific feature selection and classifiers, and pre-trained human PMBC models. Methods: Hereby we introduce CATNAP, a customizable hierarchical cell-type annotation framework. It is fully modular: catnap_core drives the cell type annotation, given a cell type hierarchy tree, specifying which classifier and parameters shall be used for each subtree. Cell type hierarchies, model parameter presets and other configuration files, tailored to human PMBC studies, are available in catnap_preset. New models can be trained with own data or curated bundles of publicly available datasets, using catnap_pretrain. Finally, catnap_evaluation defines standardized metrics and representations for model performance assessment and comparisons among sets of models. Any classifier can be integrated, registering new catnap_core backends. We provide backends for predictors spanning correlation-based (Spearman), distance-based (k-nearest neighbors, nearest mean centroid), classical machine learning (logistic regression, random forest, gradient tree boosting, support vector machine), probabilistic (linear discriminant analysis, scANVI) and foundation models (Geneformer). Results: CATNAP was used for training, and cell-types prediction on six human PBMC scRNA-seq datasets. A scANVI-based hierarchical model achieved 86.42% accuracy and 83.61% macro-F1 on these datasets, and 55.31% accuracy and 51.38% macro-F1 on two additional out-of-distribution datasets. Conclusions: CATNAP is a customizable hierarchical cell-type annotation framework, providing also a framework for benchmarking existing methods, and a prototyping environment for new classifiers. Future work will explore model combinations, and alternative configurations for exploiting the full potential of our customizable hierarchical framework. items.title: ENGLISH EDUCATION STUDENTS’ PERCEPTIONS OF USING AI TOOLS IN ACADEMIC WRITING: A CASE STUDY
items.abstract: The integration of generative artificial intelligence (AI) has significantly altered academic writing practices in higher education, yet its pedagogical implications for pre-service English teachers remain underexplored. This qualitative case study aimed to investigate English Education students' perceptions of utilizing AI tools in academic writing, specifically examining perceived benefits, operational challenges, and academic integrity negotiations. Ten undergraduate students, comprising eight eighth-semester and two sixth-semester students at Institut Pendidikan Indonesia, were purposively recruited. Data were gathered through an asynchronous online open-ended questionnaire and analyzed using Braun and Clarke's six-phase thematic analysis framework. The findings revealed that students utilized AI tools primarily for brainstorming, outlining, and grammatical refinement, while contending with fabricated citations, stylistic rigidity, and anxieties regarding the erosion of independent critical thinking. In negotiating academic integrity, participants practiced selective verification and established a collective ethical boundary that endorsed linguistic scaffolding while strictly proscribing unreflective wholesale text generation. ABSTRAK Integrasi kecerdasan buatan generatif (generative artificial intelligence) telah merevolusi praktik penulisan akademik di perguruan tinggi, namun pemaknaan pedagogis oleh mahasiswa calon guru bahasa Inggris masih jarang diteliti secara mendalam. Penelitian studi kasus kualitatif ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi persepsi mahasiswa Pendidikan Bahasa Inggris terhadap penggunaan perangkat kecerdasan buatan (AI tools) dalam penulisan akademik, yang berfokus pada persepsi manfaat, tantangan, dan negosiasi integritas akademik. Sebanyak sepuluh mahasiswa sarjana yang terdiri atas delapan mahasiswa Semester 8 dan dua mahasiswa Semester 6 di Institut Pendidikan Indonesia dipilih melalui teknik purposive sampling. Data dihimpun melalui kuesioner terbuka daring asinkron (asynchronous open-ended questionnaire) dan dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik enam tahap. Hasil penelitian mengungkapkan bahwa mahasiswa memanfaatkan perangkat kecerdasan buatan terutama untuk pencarian ide awal, penyusunan kerangka karangan, serta perbaikan tata bahasa, meskipun mereka menghadapi kendala berupa sitasi halusinasi, kekakuan gaya bahasa, dan kecemasan akan erosi keterampilan berpikir kritis mandiri. Dalam menegosiasikan integritas akademik, mahasiswa menerapkan adopsi selektif dengan memverifikasi rujukan ilmiah serta menyepakati batasan etis bahwa bantuan penyuntingan bahasa dapat dibenarkan, sedangkan penyalinan teks secara utuh merupakan bentuk pelanggaran.

items.title: ENGLISH TEACHERS’ PERCEPTIONS OF GENERATIVE AI USE IN TEACHING WRITING
items.abstract: This study aims to explore English teachers’ perceptions regarding the use of Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) in teaching writing at the senior high school level. A qualitative descriptive case study design was employed at a public senior high school in Garut, West Java. The participants were two experienced English teachers purposively selected based on their teaching tenure and digital tool integration. Data were gathered through semi-structured interviews, pedagogical document analysis, and observational field notes, then examined using Braun and Clarke’s six-phase thematic analysis. The analysis yielded six core themes: GenAI as a support for student writing, GenAI as a support for teaching, GenAI as a risk to independent learning, GenAI as a risk to textual authenticity, GenAI as a tool demanding responsible use, and GenAI as a challenge for writing assessment. The findings demonstrate that teachers maintain a conditional and context-dependent perception of AI integration. While teachers recognize its utility for lexical scaffolding and conceptual brainstorming, they emphasize rigorous boundary setting to prevent the erosion of learner autonomy and textual originality. ABSTRAK Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk mengeksplorasi persepsi guru bahasa Inggris terhadap pemanfaatan Generative Artificial Intelligence (GenAI) dalam pembelajaran menulis pada jenjang sekolah menengah atas. Penelitian ini menggunakan pendekatan kualitatif dengan desain studi kasus deskriptif pada sebuah SMA negeri di Garut, Jawa Barat. Partisipan terdiri atas dua orang guru bahasa Inggris berpengalaman yang dipilih secara purposif berdasarkan kriteria masa kerja dan kebiasaan memanfaatkan teknologi digital. Data dikumpulkan melalui wawancara semi-terstruktur, analisis artefak pembelajaran, dan catatan lapangan, kemudian dianalisis menggunakan analisis tematik model enam tahap Braun dan Clarke. Hasil analisis menghasilkan enam tema utama: GenAI sebagai pendukung tulisan siswa, GenAI sebagai pendukung pengajaran, GenAI sebagai risiko terhadap pembelajaran mandiri siswa, GenAI sebagai risiko terhadap keaslian tulisan, GenAI sebagai alat yang memerlukan penggunaan bertanggung jawab, dan GenAI sebagai tantangan bagi asesmen menulis. Temuan menunjukkan bahwa persepsi guru bersifat kondisional dan terikat pada konteks pedagogis di ruang kelas. Guru memandang GenAI bermanfaat untuk stimulasi kosakata dan ide awal, namun penggunaannya harus dibatasi agar tidak mengikis kemandirian berpikir serta orisinalitas karya tulis siswa.

items.title: Examining the Role of Modern Assessment Models in Enhancing Learning Motivation among Elementary School Students
items.abstract: Educational assessment at the elementary level extends beyond measuring the extent to which instructional objectives have been achieved, as it also influences students’ perceptions of their own abilities, the quality of classroom participation, and their motivation to continue learning. The present article aims to explain the role of modern assessment models in enhancing learning motivation among elementary school students and to identify the psychological and educational mechanisms underlying this relationship. This study employs a descriptive-analytical approach based on library research and a review of relevant scholarly articles. The analysis examines the characteristics of descriptive assessment, formative assessment, performance-based assessment, self-assessment, peer assessment, and portfolio assessment, with particular emphasis on constructive feedback, active participation, and attention to individual progress. Findings derived from the reviewed literature indicate that replacing exclusively grade-centered judgment with clear and process-oriented feedback can strengthen students’ sense of competence, academic self-efficacy, responsibility, and intrinsic motivation. Furthermore, opportunities to correct errors, awareness of one’s progress, and reduced pressure resulting from comparisons among students can promote more informed and active participation in learning activities. The effectiveness of these assessment models depends on teachers’ ability to establish clear criteria, accommodate individual differences, and involve families in the educational process. Accordingly, modern assessment can become a source of motivation when it is integrated continuously into the teaching process, thereby making the learning experience more meaningful.

items.title: Fresh for Which Claim? Separating evidence age, source lineage and decision scope in supplier research
items.abstract: This working paper investigates how supplier research can distinguish evidence age, source lineage and decision scope. It combines a purposive literature and standards synthesis with three separate Python demonstrations using constructed fixtures. A scope regression shows that selecting the latest assertion by field and source alone can discard a different supplier or service; partitioning by entity and scope before historical selection prevents that specific loss. The modules passed 14, 13 and 10 separate assertions, not an integrated accuracy evaluation. Scope identifiers and lineage are manually supplied. No production qualification, customer outcome or empirical supplier accuracy is established. items.title: Integrating Generative Artificial Intelligence into Financial Management Teaching: An Instructional Design for Finance Leasing
items.abstract: Financial Management courses often fall short in linking computational training with financing decision analysis. Taking finance leasing as a case, this paper explores how generative artificial intelligence (generative AI) can be brought into the classroom. The instructional design is built around a scenario in which a private hospital finances the purchase of medical equipment, and it connects rent calculation, comparison of financing alternatives, and scrutiny of decision conditions through a four-stage process: independent calculation, AI questioning, professional verification, and decision reconstruction. Students first carry out the calculations and form a preliminary financing judgment, then use generative AI to interrogate financing constraints and uncover the assumptions behind a plan, and finally verify the AI-generated content against financial principles to strengthen their argument. The design takes students' own judgments as the starting point of human-AI interaction and assigns AI the role of revealing and examining the conditions under which a financing plan holds, rather than making the decision for them. This approach offers a reference for bringing generative AI into accounting and finance courses.

items.title: Large language model responses to postoperative questions in oral and maxillofacial surgery: a comparative evaluation
items.abstract: Abstract Background Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly used as patient-facing informational tools in dentistry, but their suitability for postoperative communication in oral and maxillofacial surgery (OMFS) remains uncertain. This study compared ChatGPT-5.4 Thinking, DeepSeek-V3.2, and Gemini 3 (Thinking mode) in answering routine postoperative OMFS questions. Methods Thirty standardised open-ended postoperative questions were submitted once to each model through public web interfaces using the same neutral prompt. Three OMFS surgeons, masked to model identity, independently rated overall informational quality using an adapted 5-point Global Quality Score (GQS). Factual accuracy, completeness, and clinical safety were rated against a question-specific Reference Answer and Safety Framework; all responses were reassessed after peer review, and both rating sets were analysed. Five readability indices and user-interface latency were recorded. Friedman tests with Bonferroni-adjusted Wilcoxon post hoc tests were used. Results GQS inter-rater reliability was excellent [ICC(2,1), 0.900–0.926]. Mean GQS differed across models ( p < 0.001): Gemini 3 (Thinking mode) 4.82 ± 0.38, DeepSeek-V3.2 4.53 ± 0.49, and ChatGPT-5.4 Thinking 4.08 ± 0.64. Original accuracy and completeness ratings showed limited agreement [ICC(2,1), 0.379 and 0.272]. Factual accuracy differed in the original ratings ( p = 0.014) but not after reassessment ( p = 0.115); completeness did not differ. Of 90 responses, 89 were classified as Safe; one Gemini response on clopidogrel resumption was classified as Missed Red Flag/False Reassurance. After adjustment for word count, Gemini retained higher GQS than both other models (both p < 0.001). Gemini responses were generally more linguistically complex. Observed latency was shortest for DeepSeek-V3.2 (10.49 ± 1.95 s) and longest for Gemini (31.46 ± 11.60 s) and does not represent intrinsic model speed. Conclusions Gemini 3 (Thinking mode) achieved the highest expert-rated informational quality, but between-model differences in factual accuracy were not robust to reassessment, completeness did not differ, and one clinically consequential safety concern was identified. The findings are limited to simulated, single-turn, English-language first responses and do not establish patient comprehension or real-world safety. LLM-generated postoperative information should remain under professional oversight.

items.title: PERAN ARTIFICIAL INTELLIGENCE DAN INFRASTRUKTUR DIGITAL DALAM MENINGKATKAN KETERLIBATAN AKADEMIK DAN EFEKTIVITAS BELAJAR MAHASISWA
items.abstract: The increasing integration of Artificial Intelligence (AI) and digital technologies into higher education has created new opportunities to support the learning process. However, the effectiveness of technology utilization is not solely determined by technical availability, but also by students' active involvement in learning activities. This study aims to analyze the role of AI utilization and digital infrastructure in enhancing learning effectiveness, with student engagement serving as a mediating variable among students at Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. A quantitative survey approach was administered to 347 active students across faculties and cohorts selected through multistage stratified sampling. Data were gathered using a five-point Likert scale questionnaire and analyzed using Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) with a second-order construct through the Hierarchical Component Model. The results demonstrate that AI usage and digital infrastructure exert positive and significant effects on student engagement and learning effectiveness. Furthermore, student engagement partially mediates the effects of AI usage and digital infrastructure on learning effectiveness, with AI usage exhibiting a more dominant total contribution. ABSTRAK Perkembangan Artificial Intelligence (AI) dan teknologi digital telah memberikan peluang baru dalam mendukung proses pembelajaran di perguruan tinggi. Namun, efektivitas pemanfaatan teknologi tidak hanya ditentukan oleh ketersediaan fasilitas semata, melainkan juga oleh keterlibatan aktif mahasiswa dalam proses akademik. Penelitian ini bertujuan untuk menganalisis peran pemanfaatan AI dan infrastruktur digital dalam meningkatkan efektivitas belajar dengan keterlibatan mahasiswa (student engagement) sebagai variabel mediasi pada mahasiswa Institut Teknologi Kalimantan. Pendekatan kuantitatif dengan metode survei diterapkan kepada 347 mahasiswa aktif dari berbagai fakultas dan angkatan yang dipilih melalui teknik multistage stratified sampling. Pengumpulan data menggunakan kuesioner skala Likert lima tingkat dan dianalisis menggunakan Partial Least Squares–Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) dengan model konstruk tingkat kedua melalui Hierarchical Component Model. Hasil penelitian menunjukkan bahwa penggunaan AI dan infrastruktur digital berpengaruh positif dan signifikan terhadap keterlibatan mahasiswa serta efektivitas belajar.
